key_insight: Noise-biased spin qudits can make dynamical decoupling far more efficient, cutting sequence overhead from quadratic to roughly linear in dimension while preserving nonclassical states.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical route to longer-lived logical qubits in higher-dimensional hardware, improving quantum memory and error-suppression efficiency without requiring full error correction.
method: Use a d=8 antimony donor nuclear-spin qudit in silicon as the test platform.
Apply dynamical decoupling sequences adapted to the system’s biased noise.
Benchmark coherence on uniform superpositions, cat states, and Haar-random states.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports coherence improvements of about 5x to 10x, with spin-cat logical |+>_L coherence extending to 225 ms versus 19 ms in free evolution and 85 ms with Hahn echo.
watch_item: The approach depends on strong noise bias and hardware-specific sequence design, so the gain may not generalize directly to all qudit platforms.
paper_title: Dynamical Decoupling of Nonclassical States in a Biased-Noise Spin Qudit
